transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello — do you have any questions about your cataract surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi, yes, I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can go back to light exercise after 1 week, and that includes gardening. Just avoid heavy work or lifting for a month. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for that. My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: If you were using eye drops or eye gel before your operation, it’s safe to continue using them unless you were told otherwise. If you’re running out, your GP should be able to provide more. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That's helpful to know. I'm also wondering, I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: A bit of sensitivity to light can be normal while your eyes adjust. If it’s only mild, wearing sunglasses outside should help. But strong pain with bright light, or a very red and painful eye, is not normal and may need checking. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, one more. Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It’s common for vision not to be completely clear in the first week after the operation, and it should improve and settle down over time. If it’s still blurry, or getting worse, it may need checking. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that's all my questions for now. Thank you so much for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have all your questions been answered?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they have. Thanks again for your assistance!

verdict.label: pass
